case_scope.source_excerpt:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. Pass the dimensionless numerical inverse temperature $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$ and numerical energy $\widehat H_N=H_N/E_0$ to the mathematical partition definitions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; for finite energies, $\widehat\beta\widehat H_N=\beta H_N$. For the periodic energy defined below, use the same conversion $\widehat H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/E_0$. Infinite-energy configurations receive zero positive-temperature weight without evaluating $\beta(+\infty)$. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], with $d\geq2$ as stated in this physical scope. The boundary $\partial\Lambda$ is the topological boundary in the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb R^d$, and $\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda)=\inf_{y\in\partial\Lambda}|x-y|_2$. For a bounded measurable region $\Lambda$, define its two-sided layer of width $s>0$ by
$$\partial_s\Lambda=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda)\leq s\}.$$
A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $0<|\Lambda_k|<\infty$, $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$, and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\partial_s\Lambda_k|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is the two-sided Euclidean boundary-layer condition used by the mathematical shape suppliers; it controls points on both sides of $\partial\Lambda_k$. Increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with dimensionless volume $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. A configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$ is locally finite if $|\zeta\cap K|<\infty$ for every bounded set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. For such $\zeta$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. The parameter $t$ is dimensionless. Given $0\leq t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$ and $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y).$$
This sum is well-defined in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. Indeed, Cauchy--Schwarz and the defining bound for $\Omega(t)$ give $|\zeta\cap\Lambda_m|\leq\sqrt t\,V_m=O_t(m^d)$. Since $\omega$ is finite and bounded, for each fixed $x\in\omega$ and all sufficiently large dyadic shells $2^k\leq |y|_2<2^{k+1}$, one has $|x-y|_2\geq c2^k$ for some $c>0$. The absolute interaction on that shell is at most a constant times $2^{kd}\psi(c2^k)$. These bounds are summable: monotonicity gives $\int_{c2^{k-1}}^{c2^k}r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr\geq C_d2^{kd}\psi(c2^k)$ for a constant $C_d>0$, and the tail integral is finite. Only finitely many near exterior points remain; if one contributes $+\infty$, set $W_n=+\infty$, and otherwise the near sum and absolutely convergent tail define $W_n$. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

Given $N_n\in\mathbb N_0$, a reduced configuration-energy center $e\in\mathbb R$ joules per dimensionless reference volume, and a width $\delta_n>0$ in the same units, define
$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$

$$M_n(A)=\frac{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(A\cap S_n)}{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)}.$$

For the pair potential $\varphi$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$. A finite configuration is hard-admissible if every pair displacement avoids $B$. For $z>0$, define the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature free-wall weight of $\omega$ to be
$$w_0(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\{H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)<\infty\}}.$$
Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

For a periodic cell of side $L$ in dimensionless coordinates, use the exact image energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Its periodic retained-admissibility weight is
$$w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)<+\infty\}}=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{\varphi(y-x)<+\infty\text{ for every }x\in\omega,\ y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x\}}.$$
Thus every forbidden pair between distinct particles and every forbidden periodic-image pair, including a particle with one of its own nontrivial images, receives zero weight. When finite, the corresponding partition sum is $\Xi_{L}^{\mathrm{ret},0,\mathrm{per}}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}\,d\mu_{\Lambda_L,N}$. This is the periodic retained-admissibility convention; it is not an unrestricted zero-beta limit of a shell law.

citations.quote:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. Pass the dimensionless numerical inverse temperature $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$ and numerical energy $\widehat H_N=H_N/E_0$ to the mathematical partition definitions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; for finite energies, $\widehat\beta\widehat H_N=\beta H_N$. For the periodic energy defined below, use the same conversion $\widehat H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/E_0$. Infinite-energy configurations receive zero positive-temperature weight without evaluating $\beta(+\infty)$. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1], the physical positional partition sum is $\Xi_L(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda_L,N}$. Set $\alpha=\log z$; then $z^N=e^{\alpha N}$. Translate the centered cube by $L/2$ in each coordinate to $[0,L)^d$; this preserves Lebesgue measure and every pair displacement, so the positional partition is exactly the free-cube sum of [L1]. The dimensionless energy conversion in [F1] matches its numerical $\widehat\beta$. To verify the all-radius lower-regularity hypothesis of [L1], apply stability to the two-point configuration $\{0,x\}$: $\widehat\varphi(x)\ge-2\widehat B$ for $x\ne0$. Choose a finite $C\ge\max\{2\widehat B,\widehat\psi(R),0\}$ also satisfying $\widehat\varphi(0)\ge-C$; this is possible since that value is real or $+\infty$. Define $\Psi(r)=C$ for $0\le r<R$ and $\Psi(r)=\widehat\psi(r)$ for $r\ge R$. Then $\Psi$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing, $\widehat\varphi(x)\ge-\Psi(|x|_\infty)$ everywhere, and $\int_0^\infty\Psi(r)r^{d-1}dr=CR^d/d+\int_R^\infty\widehat\psi(r)r^{d-1}dr<\infty$. Together with the maximum-norm upper-tail bound in [F1], this supplies the exact regularity required by [L1].

The conditional conclusion of [L1] gives a finite limit $P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$ for $|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L$. Multiplying by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$, which is independent of $L$, converts the dimensionless reference-volume rate to pressure per physical volume.

Assume AC. Let $d\geq2$, $\varphi$ be stable with the regular integrable tail of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and assume its dimensionless representative $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable, as required by the current mathematical supplier. Take $T>0$ and $z>0$ as in [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]], set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$. For cubes $\Lambda_L=[-L/2,L/2)^d$, let $\Xi_L(z,\beta)$ be the free-wall grand partition function specified by [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Then the positional grand pressure per physical $d$-volume
$p_L(z,T)=\frac{k_BT}{\ell_0^d|\Lambda_L|}\log\Xi_L(z,\beta)$
has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. Its units are $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$; for $d=3$ this is SI pressure in pascals. In the dimensionless reference-volume convention of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], let $P(\alpha,\widehat\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\widehat\beta)$, where the supplier uses numerical energies in units of $E_0$. citations.quote:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. Pass the dimensionless numerical inverse temperature $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$ and numerical energy $\widehat H_N=H_N/E_0$ to the mathematical partition definitions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; for finite energies, $\widehat\beta\widehat H_N=\beta H_N$. For the periodic energy defined below, use the same conversion $\widehat H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/E_0$. Infinite-energy configurations receive zero positive-temperature weight without evaluating $\beta(+\infty)$. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For the pair potential $\varphi$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$. A finite configuration is hard-admissible if every pair displacement avoids $B$. For $z>0$, define the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature free-wall weight of $\omega$ to be
$$w_0(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\{H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)<\infty\}}.$$
Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

For a periodic cell of side $L$ in dimensionless coordinates, use the exact image energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Its periodic retained-admissibility weight is
$$w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)<+\infty\}}=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{\varphi(y-x)<+\infty\text{ for every }x\in\omega,\ y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x\}}.$$
Thus every forbidden pair between distinct particles and every forbidden periodic-image pair, including a particle with one of its own nontrivial images, receives zero weight. When finite, the corresponding partition sum is $\Xi_{L}^{\mathrm{ret},0,\mathrm{per}}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}\,d\mu_{\Lambda_L,N}$. This is the periodic retained-admissibility convention; it is not an unrestricted zero-beta limit of a shell law.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ and activity $z>0$, with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Select exactly one parameter branch: either a finite temperature $T>0$ in kelvins with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, or the formal retained-hard-admissibility parameter $\beta=0$, to which no finite temperature is assigned. In the mathematical numerical-energy convention use $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$; the two branches correspond to $\widehat\beta>0$ and $\widehat\beta=0$, respectively. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. After energy conversion, $\widehat\varphi_s=\varphi_s/E_0$ is stable and $\widehat\varphi_r=\varphi_r/E_0\geq0$ with core lower bound $\epsilon/E_0$, exactly as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. For each bounded Borel $A$, write $D_A(P)=D(P_A\|Q_A)$ using [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_A\ll Q_A$ and $h_A=dP_A/dQ_A$, then $D_A(P)=\int h_A\log h_A\,dQ_A$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D_A(P)=+\infty$. Let $C_0=[0,1)^d$ and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. Define $\rho(P)=E_PN_{C_0}$ and let $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ be the stationary laws with finite intensity $\rho(P)<\infty$. For $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, define each of the following quantities when its own limit exists and is finite; existence or finiteness of $I(P)$ does not require existence or finiteness of $\Phi(P)$:
$$
I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_{\Lambda_L}(P)}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.
$$
Here $I(P)$ and $\rho(P)$ are dimensionless per dimensionless reference volume; the physical number density corresponding to $\rho(P)$ is $\rho(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. The energy density $\Phi(P)$ is in joules per dimensionless reference volume; the corresponding energy density per physical $d$-volume is $\Phi(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$.
For $\beta>0$, use the laws $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For a regular potential and sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. Under this regularity hypothesis, the far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where the tuple notation means $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=H_\phi(\{q_1,\ldots,q_N\})$ when the coordinates are distinct, and $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=+\infty$ on collision diagonals. The integrand is therefore zero on collisions; these diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero by the no-collision construction in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], so this convention leaves all partition integrals unchanged. For $N=0$ the empty tuple has energy zero. Here $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], stationarity means $P\circ T_x^{-1}=P$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$. When $P$ is stationary and $E_PN_{[0,1)^d}<\infty$ (finite intensity), write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D$ defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. $$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$

$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define

with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. Here $\rho$ is particle count per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical number density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length and let $\widehat e\in\mathbb R$ be a numerical energy per dimensionless reference volume. If $\widehat\beta>0$, take $\beta=\widehat\beta/E_0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $T=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}\widehat\beta)>0$ in kelvins. If $\widehat\beta=0$, use only the formal retained-hard-admissibility branch below; it is not a finite-temperature preparation.

$$A_n=\{\omega:N_{\Lambda_n}(\omega)/V_n\in D,\ H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/(E_0V_n)\leq\widehat e\},$$
where $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ is the physical positional energy in joules with the image convention of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Equivalently, the upper-energy event is $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n\leq e$. Assume the singleton-minimizer postulate [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]] holds on its stated finite-intensity stationary-law domain at this exact supplier-selected multiplier pair and branch.

For either branch, [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] gives eventual event positivity, the constrained entropy-rate limit, and common-minimizer accumulation points; at $\widehat\beta=0$, [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]] identifies the matching retained grand law and minimizer set. Under the stated singleton assumption, both the conditioned laws and the corresponding periodic grand laws converge locally to $P^*$ for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region $A$ and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$. The energy-density center $e$ and widths for this model are in joules per dimensionless reference volume; the corresponding physical $d$-volume density has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$. This is an interval-density and upper-energy result, not a fixed-particle-number or shrinking-shell theorem.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. Pass the dimensionless numerical inverse temperature $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$ and numerical energy $\widehat H_N=H_N/E_0$ to the mathematical partition definitions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; for finite energies, $\widehat\beta\widehat H_N=\beta H_N$. For the periodic energy defined below, use the same conversion $\widehat H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/E_0$. Infinite-energy configurations receive zero positive-temperature weight without evaluating $\beta(+\infty)$. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Use the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra on $\Lambda^N$. For $N\geq1$, let
$$D_{\Lambda,N}=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\Lambda^N:x_i\ne x_j\text{ whenever }i\ne j\},\qquad \mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}=D_{\Lambda,N}/S_N,$$
where the permutation group $S_N$ acts by relabelling coordinates. Give $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ the quotient sigma-algebra: $A\subseteq\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable exactly when its preimage under the quotient map $q_N:D_{\Lambda,N}\to\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable in the trace of the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra. Identify each orbit with its unordered simple configuration. For $N=0$, set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,0}=\{\varnothing\}$. If $\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}$ is product Lebesgue measure restricted to $D_{\Lambda,N}$, define the sector reference measure by
$$\mu_{\Lambda,N}=\frac1{N!}(q_N)_\#\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}\quad(N\geq1),\qquad \mu_{\Lambda,0}(\{\varnothing\})=1.$$
Equivalently, for every nonnegative measurable function $f$ on $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$,
$$\int f(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)=\frac1{N!}\int_{D_{\Lambda,N}}f(q_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N))\,d^{dN}x.$$
Collision diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero, so $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$; in particular, symmetric integrands may use the equivalent integral over all of $\Lambda^N$. Thus $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ is a finite measure, not generally a probability. Two labelled tuples represent the same state exactly when they are in one $S_N$ orbit. The factor $1/N!$ is an adopted indistinguishable-particle positional convention, not a theorem about classical trajectories or every classical description.

Let $\mathcal C_\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{N\geq0}\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ with the disjoint-union sigma-algebra, and regard each $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ as a measure on this union supported on its $N$-point sector. Define the unit-intensity finite-region Poisson reference by
$$Q_\Lambda=e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\mu_{\Lambda,N}.$$
Its total mass is one because $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$ and $e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N\geq0}|\Lambda|^N/N!=1$. This is a positional reference measure in the chosen dimensionless coordinates; it supplies no empirical claim about particle trajectories.

Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], fix $\beta>0$, and define $Z(L,N;\beta)$ as in that definition. For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$. On the interior of $\{\rho:F(\rho)>-\infty\}$, $F$ is finite and continuous. For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1] and [F2], the free-wall partition on $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ is precisely the activity sum over the canonical positional sectors used in [L2], with $\alpha=\log z$; [F1] and [L1] supply the stable-tail hypotheses and the canonical rate $F$ on its interior. In the mathematical partition, $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ and $\widehat H=H/E_0$, so the Boltzmann factors agree.
The conditional mathematical conclusion [L2] gives both displayed Legendre–Fenchel identities, including only the stipulated closed concave endpoint extension.

Multiplication by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$ converts the dimensionless log-partition rate to physical pressure, while multiplication of the canonical rate by $-k_BT/\ell_0^d$ gives the stated positional free-energy density; the common measure normalization is fixed by [F2]. Since [L2] is a statement about thermodynamic functions, it supplies no local convergence or phase-uniqueness claim.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Assume AC and $T>0$, with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and take $z>0$ as in [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Under the stable regularly tempered positional model of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]] and the adopted ensemble weights of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]], assume the dimensionless potential $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable as required by the current mathematical carriers. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$; write $F(\rho,\beta)$ and $P(\alpha,\beta)$ for the mathematical rates evaluated at $\widehat\beta$. Use free-wall cubes $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ with dimensionless volume $V_L=L^d$. Write $Z_L(N;\beta)=\int e^{-\beta H_N}\,d\mu_{\Lambda_L,N}$, extending the integrand by zero at infinite energy, for their canonical positional partitions. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ be the canonical log-partition rate per dimensionless reference volume, defined on positive interior attainable densities by $V_L^{-1}\log Z_L(N_L;\beta)\to F(\rho,\beta)$ for every sequence $N_L/V_L\to\rho$ and extended to the closed effective density domain by the upper-semicontinuous concave extension specified in [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], with $F(\rho,\beta)=-\infty$ outside that closed domain. Let
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}\log\sum_{N\geq0}e^{\alpha N}Z_L(N;\beta),\qquad \alpha=\log z.$$
Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\{F(\rho,\beta)+\alpha\rho\},$$
and, for every $\rho$ in the closed effective density domain of $F$,
$$F(\rho,\beta)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\{P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\}.$$
The density $\rho$ is particle count per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical number density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. In physical units, $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P$ and the positional Helmholtz free-energy density is $f_{\mathrm{pos}}=-(k_BT/\ell_0^d)F$; both are per physical $d$-volume, in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$ (pascals when $d=3$). The fixed $1/N!$ reference normalization is that of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This duality concerns limiting thermodynamic functions only. It does not imply local ensemble equivalence, uniqueness of a phase, or convergence at excluded density endpoints.

citations.quote:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. Pass the dimensionless numerical inverse temperature $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$ and numerical energy $\widehat H_N=H_N/E_0$ to the mathematical partition definitions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; for finite energies, $\widehat\beta\widehat H_N=\beta H_N$. For the periodic energy defined below, use the same conversion $\widehat H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/E_0$. Infinite-energy configurations receive zero positive-temperature weight without evaluating $\beta(+\infty)$. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, its side length $L_n=2n+1$ and dimensionless volume $V_n=L_n^d$, the periodic positional energy $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the exact-$N$ measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. Given $N_n\in\mathbb N_0$, a reduced configuration-energy center $e\in\mathbb R$ joules per dimensionless reference volume, and a width $\delta_n>0$ in the same units, define
$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$
When $0<\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)<\infty$, the uniform positional shell law is
$$M_n(A)=\frac{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(A\cap S_n)}{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)}.$$
A shrinking energy-density shell uses some specified sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$. Its total energy width is $2\delta_nV_n$, which is $o(V_n)$ but need not be microscopic or bounded. Existence of a normalizing shell and the existence of a suitable shrinking sequence are separate theorem obligations. This is not a surface measure on an exact-energy hypersurface and not a phase-space shell for $K(p)+H_N^{\mathrm{per}}$.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ and activity $z>0$, with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Select exactly one parameter branch: either a finite temperature $T>0$ in kelvins with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, or the formal retained-hard-admissibility parameter $\beta=0$, to which no finite temperature is assigned. In the mathematical numerical-energy convention use $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$; the two branches correspond to $\widehat\beta>0$ and $\widehat\beta=0$, respectively. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. After energy conversion, $\widehat\varphi_s=\varphi_s/E_0$ is stable and $\widehat\varphi_r=\varphi_r/E_0\geq0$ with core lower bound $\epsilon/E_0$, exactly as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. For each bounded Borel $A$, write $D_A(P)=D(P_A\|Q_A)$ using [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_A\ll Q_A$ and $h_A=dP_A/dQ_A$, then $D_A(P)=\int h_A\log h_A\,dQ_A$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D_A(P)=+\infty$. Let $C_0=[0,1)^d$ and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. Define $\rho(P)=E_PN_{C_0}$ and let $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ be the stationary laws with finite intensity $\rho(P)<\infty$. For $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, define each of the following quantities when its own limit exists and is finite; existence or finiteness of $I(P)$ does not require existence or finiteness of $\Phi(P)$:
$$
I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_{\Lambda_L}(P)}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.
$$
Here $I(P)$ and $\rho(P)$ are dimensionless per dimensionless reference volume; the physical number density corresponding to $\rho(P)$ is $\rho(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. The energy density $\Phi(P)$ is in joules per dimensionless reference volume; the corresponding energy density per physical $d$-volume is $\Phi(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$.
For $\beta>0$, use the laws $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For a regular potential and sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. Under this regularity hypothesis, the far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where the tuple notation means $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=H_\phi(\{q_1,\ldots,q_N\})$ when the coordinates are distinct, and $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=+\infty$ on collision diagonals. The integrand is therefore zero on collisions; these diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero by the no-collision construction in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], so this convention leaves all partition integrals unchanged. For $N=0$ the empty tuple has energy zero. Here $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], stationarity means $P\circ T_x^{-1}=P$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$. When $P$ is stationary and $E_PN_{[0,1)^d}<\infty$ (finite intensity), write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D$ defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. If $\phi$ is stable with constant $B$, then $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}\geq-BN_{\Lambda_L}$, so the negative part of $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ is $P$-integrable for every such $P$. Whenever the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
In the variational results below, $\Phi(P)$ denotes this same positional energy density: $\Phi(P):=\mathcal E(P)$. The cited results establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume either limit exists for every stationary finite-intensity law.
